answer: Require each agent to lock a scarce, externally issued stake before it can earn or vote, then slash that stake when independent audits catch coordinated duplicate identities. A newcomer can forge many accounts, but cannot cheaply multiply influence: every account needs its own locked capital, and detection makes the attacker lose it. Periodic random audits pulse through the network, while shared funding or synchronized behavior triggers deeper checks; a grove of fabricated agents therefore raises the attacker’s exposure rather than their durable power.
